label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They score well below typical thresholds on all three psychological distress measures (UCLA-8 loneliness mean ≈ 0.81, PHQ-9 depression mean ≈ 0.32, GAD-7 anxiety mean ≈ 0.04), suggesting a generally positive mental health status with minimal psychological distress.

label: High-Distress Heavy-Screen-Time Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily on screens and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (mean 1.72), PHQ-9 depression score (mean 1.76), and GAD-7 anxiety score (mean 2.18) are all in the higher range, indicating a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress across all three domains, with anxiety being the most pronounced.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen time
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale
Endorses elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9
Exhibits the highest distress on anxiety measures (GAD-7 mean 2.18)
Engages in heavy daily screen use exceeding 5 hours
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggests compounding psychological burden
tone: Clinically concerned and empathetic; acknowledges significant multi-dimensional distress

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With mean scores well below clinical thresholds on all three measures (UCLA-8 loneliness: 1.25, PHQ-9 depression: 0.82, GAD-7 anxiety: 0.85), these individuals demonstrate robust psychological well-being. They are characterized by moderate daily screen or internet use (1–3 hours) and higher educational attainment.
